interest: This docket list offers a valuable institutional index tracking how the U.S. Foreign Service monitored Japanese immigration policy, labor restrictions, and alien control measures throughout the 1930s. It highlights diplomatic sensitivity surrounding shipping and harbor police authority through the 1933 detention of the American Mail Line steamship S.S. President Jefferson in Yokohama, as well as Japanese scrutiny of foreign performers, exemplified by the eviction of the Hawaiian Kaili Troupe. Additionally, it documents interactions between academic research and government intelligence through historian Samuel Flagg Bemis's inquiries regarding Japanese alien land ownership, and records the tightening of national security and border controls through the Home Department's 1939 ordinances on alien entry, sojourn, and departure.
overview: This file consists of the Department of State's three-page 'List of Papers' (docket sheet and register) for decimal classification 894.55, titled 'Japan, Immigration. Head Tax.' covering entries from March 1931 through June 1939. The docket lists twenty recorded sub-files, including diplomatic despatches, consular reports, cross-reference sheets, and internal State Department memoranda concerning Japanese immigration laws and regulations governing the admission, temporary residence, and employment of aliens. Notable matters indexed include the regulation of alien entry into Japan and its South Sea Mandated Islands, the detention and quiet settlement of the American Mail Line steamship S.S. President Jefferson by Yokohama harbor police in 1933, consular surveys from Tokyo, Nagasaki, Kobe, Nagoya, and Taihoku on the admission of alien entertainers and musicians (including the eviction of the Kaili Troupe), inquiries by historian Samuel Flagg Bemis on alien land ownership and immigration enforcement, and the promulgation of new Japanese Home Department ordinances regulating alien entry, sojourn, and departure in 1939. Because the underlying substantive documents were cross-referenced and filed under other decimal classifications (notably 894.111 and 800.504), this register serves as the complete surviving record under file 894.55.

subfiles.summary: This three-page administrative register indexes communications and consular reports filed under State Department decimal file 894.55 between March 31, 1931, and June 19, 1939. It summarizes dispatches concerning laws regulating alien entry into Japan and the South Sea Mandated Islands, the detention and diplomatic adjustment of the American Mail Line ship S.S. President Jefferson at Yokohama, and widespread consular reports on alien employment and entertainers, specifically referencing the eviction of the Kaili Troupe. Additionally, it records correspondence with historian Samuel Flagg Bemis regarding Japanese alien land tenure and immigration enforcement, followed by the promulgation and translation of the 1939 Home Department ordinances governing alien entry, sojourn, and departure.
